meta.probingQuestion: Have you ever broken something with someone and left it broken?

games.title: Stick and Pull Foot Sweep Game
Closed Guard Opening — Hands on Body
Head and Arm Strangle — Close Position Start

meta.connection: A finish you can apply and release on the tap is power you control. Leaving a break unrepaired is choosing not to release, not to reset. The tap is the invitation to repair. This week asks whether you take it.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, closed guard, and mount. On the mat, a finish is only safe if you let go the second your partner taps. Letting go is a choice you control. Fixing something broken between two people is a choice too.

slides.title: Have you ever broken something with someone and left it broken?

body.text: Stick and Pull Foot Sweep Game
This is a foot trip from a standing clinch.

items: The overhook player wins by putting the underhook player on a knee or his back.
The underhook player wins by lifting the overhook player, getting behind him, or picking up his leg.

body.text: Closed Guard Opening — Hands on Body
This is standing up to open legs locked around your waist.

items: The top player wins by getting to his feet and opening the guard.
The bottom player wins by stopping the top player's win for 30 seconds. Then switch.

body.text: Head and Arm Strangle — Close Position Start
This is trapping the head and one arm together.

items: The top player wins with the arm trapped at the head.
The bottom player wins by pulling his own trapped elbow back against his body, or by bridging and rolling the top player off.

slides.title: What would you do?
slides.question: You're building a strangle from your partner's back, and your arm has just touched him. What's the smart move?

options.text: Keep that arm right where it landed.
options.feedback: Keeping the arm in place takes the same patience as fixing a break.

options.text: Pull the arm back to make more space.
options.feedback: Pulling back loses the finish you just started.

options.text: Switch your grip to his head instead.
options.feedback: The finish starts on his back, not his head.
